strategyBlocks.value: Square each domain element to get its image, list the results as ordered pairs, then read the domain and range from the two sets and apply the definition of a function.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (c) {(−2, 4), (−1, 1), (0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 4)}  (d) Domain = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2}  (e) Range = {0, 1, 4}  (f) It is a function because every element of the domain has exactly one image — no input is mapped to two different outputs.

whyThisWorks.value: A relation is a function when each input is assigned one and only one output; nothing forbids two different inputs sharing an output. Here −2 and 2 both map to 4, and −1 and 1 both map to 1, yet each individual input still has a single arrow leaving it, so the definition is satisfied. Sets list each element once, which is why the range has three members even though five arrows are drawn.

commonErrors.misconception: Listing 1 and 4 twice in the range because two arrows point to each.
